guarantees.claim: For share index 0, irregular[0] is assigned rcon_added when use_rcon is true, otherwise sub_word_out.
For share indices 1 to NumShares-1, irregular[s] is assigned sw_out_mask.

assumptions.claim: sw_out_mask must correctly provide the mask share for the current key expansion round when NumShares > 1.
assumptions.risk: If sw_out_mask is incorrect, the produced mask share irregular[s] (s>0) will be wrong, compromising the masked key schedule and potentially enabling side-channel leakage.

uncertain_points.claim: When use_rcon is false, irregular[0] gets sub_word_out. It is unclear whether sub_word_out is already masked (as suggested by comment 'The (masked) key share') or is raw data. If already masked, then combining with sw_out_mask for other shares may break the masking scheme (e.g., double masking or incorrect mask application).
uncertain_points.risk: Masking integrity could be violated, potentially enabling side-channel attacks on the key expansion.

uncertain_points.claim: For all shares s>0, the same mask value sw_out_mask is assigned to irregular[s]. In typical masking, each share should be an independent random value. Using the same mask for multiple shares may reduce the security level and increase correlation between shares.
uncertain_points.risk: Masked implementation may not provide intended side-channel resistance, potentially leaking key information.

uncertain_points.claim: If NumShares is set to 1, the generate loop only produces share 0 with no mask share, effectively disabling masking. This may be an allowed non-masked configuration, but could be a security risk if not intended.
uncertain_points.risk: Key expansion would operate without any mask, exposing raw key material to side-channel attacks.
